slot.brief: Simple fact recall on diborane structure (banana bonds, electron-deficient nature) or boron family anomaly; one-liner definition question.

stem: Which statement correctly describes the bonding in diborane, $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$?
options: It contains two three-centre, two-electron B–H–B bonds.
It contains only ordinary two-centre, two-electron bonds.
It contains ionic B–H bonds formed by complete electron transfer.
It contains two three-centre, four-electron B–H–B bonds.

verdicts.working: Diborane has two bridging B–H–B bonds, each a three-centre, two-electron bond; the terminal B–H bonds are ordinary two-centre bonds.

working:
Each bridging B–H–B unit in diborane is a three-centre, two-electron bond.
